questions.question: Sa pangungusap na “Malamig ang simoy ng hangin,” ano ang pinakamalapit na kahulugan ng “simoy”?

choices.A: Banayad na daloy ng hangin
choices.B: Direksiyong tinatahak ng hangin
choices.C: Amoy na dala ng hangin
choices.D: Tunog na nalilikha ng hangin

questions.note: Ang simoy ay banayad na ihip o daloy ng hangin.

questions.question: Alin ang wastong paggamit ng “nang” upang ilarawan ang paraan ng pagkilos?

choices.A: Nang dumating siya, nagsimula ang pulong.
choices.B: Tumakbo siya nang mabilis.
choices.C: Umalis siya nang tanghali.
choices.D: Naglakad siya ng mabilis.

questions.note: Ginagamit ang “nang” upang ilarawan kung paano isinagawa ang kilos; maaari rin itong mag-ugnay ng sugnay sa ibang gamit.

questions.question: Ano ang pinakamalapit na kahulugan ng sawikaing “makapal ang mukha” kapag sinabing “Makapal ang mukha niya at humingi pa rin ng pabor matapos manloko”?

choices.A: Katapatan sa pagsasabi ng sariling saloobin.
choices.B: Pagiging mapagbigay sa oras ng pangangailangan.
choices.C: Kawalan ng hiya kahit may maling ginawa.
choices.D: Lakas ng loob sa harap ng pisikal na panganib.

questions.note: Ang “makapal ang mukha” ay tumutukoy sa kawalan ng hiya o pag-aalinlangan kahit may ginawang mali.

questions.question: Sa anatomikal na gamit, saan matatagpuan ang siko?

choices.A: Sa dugtungan ng balikat at itaas na braso
choices.B: Sa dugtungan ng bisig at palad
choices.C: Sa dugtungan ng itaas na braso at bisig
choices.D: Sa dugtungan ng hita at binti

questions.note: Ang siko ay kasukasuan sa pagitan ng itaas na braso at bisig.

questions.question: Kung inilalarawan ang pagkain bilang “masarap,” anong katangian ang tinutukoy?

choices.A: Mataas ang sustansiya
choices.B: Kaaya-aya ang lasa
choices.C: Mahal ang halaga
choices.D: Matagal bago masira

questions.note: Ang “masarap” ay tumutukoy sa kaaya-ayang lasa.

questions.question: Anong bilang ang tinutukoy ng salitang “apatnapu”?
questions.note: Ang apatnapu ay katumbas ng 40.

questions.question: Alin ang salitang tumutukoy sa kalipunan ng maliliit na patak ng tubig o kristal ng yelo na nakikita sa himpapawid?

choices.A: Usok
choices.B: Hamog
choices.C: Ambon
choices.D: Ulap

questions.note: Ang ulap ay binubuo ng maliliit na patak ng tubig o kristal ng yelo na nakalutang sa atmospera.

questions.question: Alin ang kasalungat ng “mabigat” kapag tinutukoy ang timbang?

choices.A: Matibay
choices.B: Makapal
choices.C: Malambot
choices.D: Magaan

questions.note: Ang kasalungat ng mabigat sa usapin ng timbang ay magaan.

questions.question: Ano ang tawag sa anak ng iyong kapatid?

choices.A: Pamangkin
choices.B: Bayaw
choices.C: Inaanak
choices.D: Pinsan

questions.note: Ang anak ng kapatid ay pamangkin.

questions.question: Sa pangungusap na “Babalik ako bukas,” ano ang kahulugan ng “bukas”?

choices.A: Ngayon
choices.B: Kinabukasan
choices.C: Kahapon
choices.D: Mamayang gabi

questions.note: Sa pangungusap na ito, ang “bukas” ay tumutukoy sa susunod na araw.

questions.question: Ano ang pangunahing pagkakaiba ng “Nagsulat si Lira ng liham” at “Sinulatan ni Lira ang guro”?

choices.A: Sa una, walang pandiwa; sa ikalawa, may pandiwa
choices.B: Sa una, ang liham ang tagaganap; sa ikalawa, ang guro ang sumulat
choices.C: Sa una, naganap ang kilos; sa ikalawa, magaganap pa lamang ito
choices.D: Sa una, si Lira ang pokus; sa ikalawa, ang taong sinulatan ang binibigyang-diin

questions.note: Nasa pokus sa tagaganap ang “nagsulat”; sa “sinulatan,” binibigyang-diin ang taong sinulatan.

questions.question: Sa “Hindi siya sumama, bagkus ay nagpaiwan,” ano ang tungkulin ng “bagkus”?

choices.A: Pagbibigay ng isang halimbawa
choices.B: Pagpapalit o pagwawasto sa inaasahang kilos
choices.C: Pagpapakita ng pagkakasunod ng oras
choices.D: Pagpapaliwanag ng dahilan

questions.note: Ipinakikita ng “bagkus” ang pagpapalit o pagwawasto sa unang ideya.

questions.question: Aling pangungusap ang wastong gumagamit ng “kung” bilang pangatnig at “kong” bilang pinaikling “ko” na sinusundan ng pang-angkop?

choices.A: Kung may oras ako, babasahin ko ang aklat kung bago.
choices.B: Kong may oras ako, babasahin ko ang aklat kong bago.
choices.C: Kong may oras ako, babasahin ko ang aklat kung bago.
choices.D: Kung may oras ako, babasahin ko ang aklat kong bago.

questions.note: Ang “kung” ay pangatnig para sa kondisyon; ang “kong” ay pinagsanib na “ko” at pang-angkop na “-ng.”

questions.question: Sa “Ipinagluto ni Ana ng lugaw ang maysakit,” sino ang nakinabang sa kilos?

choices.A: Ang lugaw
choices.B: Si Ana
choices.C: Ang maysakit
choices.D: Ang taong nag-utos kay Ana

questions.note: Ang maysakit ang benepisyaryo o taong pinaglaanan ng pagluluto.

questions.question: Ano ang pangunahing tungkulin ng “pala” sa “Ikaw pala ang bagong guro”?

choices.A: Pagpapahayag ng utos
choices.B: Pagpapahayag ng bagong natuklasan
choices.C: Pagpapakita ng pagmamay-ari
choices.D: Pagmamarka ng kilos sa hinaharap

questions.note: Ipinahihiwatig ng “pala” na may bagong nalaman o napagtanto ang nagsasalita.

questions.question: Alin ang pinakamalapit na kahulugan ng “marahuyo” kumpara sa simpleng “magustuhan”?

choices.A: Mahumaling o maakit nang matindi
choices.B: Maging magalang sa kausap
choices.C: Mabilis na magbago ng pasiya
choices.D: Maging malungkot dahil sa pangyayari

questions.note: Mas matindi ang pagkaakit o pagkabighani na ipinahihiwatig ng “marahuyo.”

questions.question: Sa “Kung hindi dahil sa babala, napahamak sana sila,” anong ugnayan ang ipinapakita?

choices.A: Paghahambing ng dalawang tao
choices.B: Magkasunod na utos
choices.C: Di-naganap na kondisyon at maaaring naging bunga
choices.D: Pagbibigay-kahulugan sa isang salita

questions.note: Ipinahihiwatig ng “kung hindi dahil” at “sana” ang kondisyong hindi nangyari at ang posibleng bunga nito.

questions.question: Ano ang ipinahihiwatig ng “umano” sa isang ulat?

choices.A: Nagbibigay ng utos ang nagsasalita
choices.B: Iniulat ito, ngunit hindi tiyak na pinagtibay
choices.C: Tahasang pinabubulaanan ang pahayag
choices.D: Tiyak na napatunayan ang pahayag

questions.note: Inilalayo ng “umano” ang nagsasalita sa ganap na pagpapatibay sa iniulat na pahayag.

questions.question: Aling pares ang pinakamahusay na naghihiwalay sa “masinop” at “maramot” sa konteksto ng paggastos?

choices.A: Masinop: maingat magplano at gumastos; maramot: umiiwas gumastos o magbahagi kahit makatuwiran.
choices.B: Masinop: umiiwas gumastos sa iba; maramot: maingat magplano at mag-ipon.
choices.C: Masinop: gumagastos agad kapag may pera; maramot: nagtatakda ng badyet bago bumili.
choices.D: Masinop: umiiwas gumastos sa sarili kahit may layunin; maramot: maingat magbadyet at gumastos ayon sa pangangailangan.

questions.note: Ang masinop ay maingat at mahusay humawak ng yaman; ang maramot ay labis na nag-aatubiling gumastos o magbahagi.

questions.question: Ano ang karaniwang ipinahihiwatig ng “Sayang!” kapag may pagkakataong nasayang?

choices.A: Panghihinayang sa nawalang pagkakataon
choices.B: Ginhawa matapos ang panganib
choices.C: Pagkamangha sa magandang balita
choices.D: Pagkagalit dahil sa insulto

questions.note: Karaniwang nagpapahayag ang “Sayang!” ng panghihinayang sa nawala o nasayang.

questions.question: Sa pangungusap na “Ikinagalit ng konseho ang pasyang ipinataw nang walang konsultasyon,” alin ang sanhi ng galit?

choices.A: Ang konsehong tumutol sa pasya
choices.B: Ang galit na naging sanhi ng pagkakaroon ng pasya
choices.C: Ang kawalan ng konsultasyon na nag-udyok sa pagtutol
choices.D: Ang taong naglabas ng pahayag tungkol sa konseho

questions.note: Sa “ikinagalit,” ang pasya at ang paraang ginamit sa pagpapataw nito ang inilalahad na sanhi ng galit.

questions.question: May taong tumanggap ng mapanganib na trabaho dahil wala na siyang ibang paraan upang makabili ng pagkain para sa pamilya. Aling sawikain ang pinakamalapit sa sitwasyon?

choices.A: Makati ang paa
choices.B: Kapit sa patalim
choices.C: Bukal sa loob
choices.D: Balat-sibuyas

questions.note: Ang “kapit sa patalim” ay tumutukoy sa desperadong hakbang na ginagawa dahil sa kagipitan.

questions.question: Sa pahayag na “Hindi dahil sa takot, kundi dahil sa paggalang siya nanahimik,” ano ang tungkulin ng “kundi”?

choices.A: Itinatanggi ang unang dahilan at inilalagay ang kapalit na paliwanag.
choices.B: Nagdaragdag ito ng isa pang dahilan na maaaring kasabay ng una.
choices.C: Ipinakikita nito ang bunga ng takot matapos ang pangyayari.
choices.D: Ipinakikita nito ang sunod-sunod na pangyayari sa salaysay.

questions.note: Sa “hindi dahil sa…, kundi dahil sa…,” itinatanggi ang unang paliwanag at inilalahad ang kapalit na dahilan.

questions.question: Sa isang talumpati, sinabing “napanatili niya ang dangal kahit hindi siya ginawaran ng karangalan.” Ano ang pinakamainam na pagbasa sa dalawang salita?

choices.A: Ang “dangal” ay higit na tumutukoy sa panlabas na pagkilala; ang “karangalan” naman sa asal at integridad.
choices.B: Maaaring tumukoy ang “dangal” sa integridad; ang “karangalan” ay maaari ring tumukoy sa pagkilalang iginagawad.
choices.C: Ang “dangal” ay tumutukoy sa katayuang panlipunan; ang “karangalan” ay sa pansariling damdamin lamang.
choices.D: Magkaugnay ang dalawang salita, ngunit laging magkapareho ang kahulugan at gamit ng mga ito.

questions.note: Magkaugnay ang mga salita, ngunit maaaring tumukoy ang “dangal” sa integridad at ang “karangalan” sa pagkilalang natatanggap.

questions.question: Paghambingin ang “Hindi pa siya handa” at “Hindi na siya handa.” Ano ang pinakamahalagang pagkakaiba?

choices.A: Ang “pa” ay nagpapahiwatig ng kondisyon, samantalang ang “na” ay ginagamit sa mga tanong.
choices.B: Pareho nilang ipinahahayag ang kawalan ng kahandaan nang walang ipinahihiwatig na pagbabago.
choices.C: Ang “pa” ay tumutukoy lamang sa nakaraan, samantalang ang “na” ay tumutukoy lamang sa hinaharap.
choices.D: “Hindi pa” ay nangangahulugang not yet; “hindi na” ay nagpapahiwatig na nagbago ang kalagayan.

questions.note: Maaaring magpahiwatig ang “pa” ng kalagayang hindi pa nagaganap, samantalang ang “na” ay madalas na nagpapahiwatig ng pagbabago o paghinto ng dating kalagayan.

questions.question: Alin ang pinakamalapit na diwa ng salawikaing “Nasa Diyos ang awa, nasa tao ang gawa” sa isang proyektong nangangailangan ng pagtutulungan?

choices.A: Ang pag-asa sa awa ay hindi kapalit ng sariling kilos at pananagutan.
choices.B: Sapat na ang mabuting hangarin kahit walang ginagawang hakbang.
choices.C: Dapat hintayin muna ang tulong bago magplano o magsimula.
choices.D: Ang pagtanggap ng tulong ay nangangahulugang hindi na kailangan ang sariling pagsisikap.

questions.note: Pinagsasama ng salawikain ang pag-asa at personal na pagkilos; hindi nito itinatanggi ang pagtutulungan.

questions.question: Sa “Ipinagkait sa mga manggagawa ang kabayarang ipinangako sa kanila,” ano ang ipinahihiwatig ng pandiwang “ipinagkait”?

choices.A: Naibigay sa mga manggagawa ang kabayarang inaasahan nila bago ang itinakdang araw.
choices.B: Tumanggi ang mga manggagawa na tanggapin ang ipinangakong kabayaran sa kanila.
choices.C: Hindi ibinigay ang bagay na inaasahan o nararapat nilang matanggap.
choices.D: Nagpasya ang mga manggagawa sa halagang matatanggap nila bilang kabayaran.

questions.note: Ipinahihiwatig ng “ipinagkait” na hindi ibinigay ang isang bagay na inaasahan o nararapat matanggap.

questions.question: Sa isang pabatid, isinulat na “pumanaw ang dating punong-guro” sa halip na “namatay ang dating punong-guro.” Ano ang pangunahing epekto ng pagpili ng salita?

choices.A: Gumagamit ito ng mas banayad na pananalita upang talakayin ang pagkamatay
choices.B: Ginagawang nakakatawa ang pangyayari sa pamamagitan ng pagpapalabis
choices.C: Inilalarawan nito ang sanhi ng pagkamatay nang mas eksakto
choices.D: Pinapalitan nito ang pahayag ng kabaligtaran nitong kahulugan

questions.note: Ang “pumanaw” ay isang eupemismo o mas banayad na pananalita para sa “namatay.”

questions.question: Sa tulang gumagamit ng “ako” na nagsasalaysay ng pagkabigo, ano ang dapat iwasan ng mambabasa kung walang ibang ebidensiya?

choices.A: Ihambing ang pananaw ng persona sa mga larawang ginamit
choices.B: Ipagpalagay na awtomatikong kapareho ng persona ang makata
choices.C: Tingnan kung paano umuunlad ang tinig sa kabuuan ng tula
choices.D: Suriin ang mga salitang nagpapahiwatig ng damdamin

questions.note: Ang persona ay tinig o katauhang nagsasalita sa tula at hindi awtomatikong katumbas ng tunay na makata.

questions.question: Sa pahayag na “Siya ang ilaw ng tahanan,” alin ang nagpapaliwanag sa metaporikal na kahulugan nito?

choices.A: Siya ang may pananagutan sa bayarin sa kuryente
choices.B: Siya ang taong karaniwang nagbubukas ng mga ilaw sa bahay
choices.C: Inilalarawan ang liwanag na nagmumula sa isang lampara
choices.D: Iniuugnay siya sa paggabay, pag-aaruga, o pag-asa sa pamilya

questions.note: Metapora ito dahil inilalarawan ang isang tao bilang pinagmumulan ng gabay o pag-asa sa pamilya.

questions.question: Sa “Ikinabahala ng mga residente ang mabilis na pagtaas ng tubig,” alin ang inilalahad bilang sanhi ng pagkabahala?

choices.A: Ang mga residenteng nagbabala sa mga kapitbahay tungkol sa panganib.
choices.B: Ang pagtitipon ng mga residente upang pag-usapan ang kalagayan ng ilog.
choices.C: Ang kakulangan ng babala mula sa mga kinauukulan bago tumaas ang tubig.
choices.D: Ang mabilis na pagtaas ng tubig.

questions.note: Sa “ikinabahala,” ang mabilis na pagtaas ng tubig ang inilalahad na sanhi ng pagkabahala.

questions.question: Aling pangungusap ang gumagamit nang wasto sa “sakaling” upang magpasok ng isang kondisyon?

choices.A: Sakaling maantala ang tren, nagsimula tayo nang mas huli.
choices.B: Sakaling maantala ang tren, dahil magsisimula tayo nang mas huli.
choices.C: Sakaling maantala ang tren, magsisimula tayo nang mas huli.
choices.D: Sakaling maantala ang tren, nagsimula sana tayo nang mas huli kahapon.

questions.note: Karaniwang sinusundan ang “sakaling” ng sugnay na naglalahad ng kondisyong maaaring mangyari.

questions.question: Sa usapan, sinabi ni Mara: “Hindi raw siya ang kumuha ng susi.” Ano ang ipinahihiwatig ng “raw” sa pahayag ni Mara?

choices.A: Iniulat ni Mara ang sinabi ng iba; hindi nito pinatutunayan ang pagtanggi.
choices.B: Tinutukoy ng “raw” kung sino ang nagmamay-ari ng susi sa pangungusap.
choices.C: Ipinahihiwatig na personal na nasaksihan ni Mara ang pagtanggi at pinagtitibay niya ito.
choices.D: Ipinakikita ng “raw” na kukunin pa lamang ang susi sa ibang pagkakataon.

questions.note: Ang “raw” ay panandang nagsasaad na iniulat o ipinasa ang pahayag mula sa ibang tao; hindi nito mismo pinatutunayan ang katotohanan nito.

questions.question: Sa “Liban si Nilo sa pulong” at “Dumating ang lahat liban kay Nilo,” bakit magkaiba ang gamit ng “liban”?

choices.A: Sa una, tumutukoy ang “liban” sa hindi pagdalo; sa ikalawa, nangangahulugang “maliban kay.”
choices.B: Sa una, ang “liban” ay pagbubukod; sa ikalawa, nangangahulugan itong hindi nakadalo si Nilo.
choices.C: Sa una, nangangahulugang wala siyang kasama; sa ikalawa, ang bilang ng dumalo ang inilalarawan.
choices.D: Sa parehong pangungusap, nangangahulugan ang “liban” na hindi pinayagan si Nilo na dumalo.

questions.note: Maaaring tumukoy ang “liban” sa hindi pagdalo o sa pagbubukod, depende sa pagkakabuo ng pangungusap.

questions.question: Sinabi ng patnugot, “Timbangin muna natin ang dalawang salaysay bago magpasya.” Ano ang hinihingi niya?

choices.A: Alisin ang magkasalungat na bahagi upang magmukhang magkatugma
choices.B: Suriin ang batayan, pagkakatugma, at pagiging maaasahan ng dalawang salaysay
choices.C: Bilangin ang mga salitang ginamit sa bawat salaysay
choices.D: Piliin agad ang salaysay na mas kapani-paniwala ang tunog

questions.note: Ginamit ang “timbangin” sa matalinghagang kahulugang maingat na suriin at paghambingin ang ebidensiya.

questions.question: Sa isang sanaysay, paulit-ulit na ginagamit ang “di-maikakaila.” Ano ang dapat unawain ng mambabasa tungkol sa pananalita?

choices.A: Ipinahihiwatig nitong may pag-aalinlangan ang may-akda sa mismong pahayag.
choices.B: Inililipat nito sa mambabasa ang pananagutan sa katotohanan ng pahayag.
choices.C: Tinitiyak nitong napagtibay ng ibang tao ang bawat pahayag na kasunod nito.
choices.D: Nagpapahayag ito ng matibay na paninindigan, ngunit kailangan pa rin ng ebidensiya.

questions.note: Malakas ang paninindigang ipinahihiwatig ng “di-maikakaila,” ngunit kailangan pa ring suriin ang batayan ng argumento.

questions.question: Sa “Hindi niya itinanggi ang paratang; gayunman, humingi siya ng pagkakataong magpaliwanag,” ano ang tungkulin ng “gayunman”?

choices.A: Nagpapakilala ito ng pagsalungat o limitasyong kailangang isaalang-alang
choices.B: Nagdaragdag ito ng kaparehong halimbawa
choices.C: Nagpapakita ito ng bunga na lohikal na kasunod ng paratang
choices.D: Nagtatakda ito ng kondisyon bago magsimula ang pangyayari

questions.note: Ang “gayunman” ay panandang nagpapakita ng pagsalungat o paglihis sa inaasahang ugnayan ng mga pahayag.

questions.question: Aling pares ang wastong gumagamit ng “raw” at “daw” ayon sa tunog na nauuna sa pantukoy ng pahayag?

choices.A: “Umalis raw siya” at “Bukas raw ang tindahan.”
choices.B: “Umalis daw siya” at “Bukas daw ang tindahan.”
choices.C: “Umalis daw siya” at “Bukas raw ang tindahan.”
choices.D: “Umalis raw siya” at “Bukas daw ang tindahan.”

questions.note: Karaniwang ginagamit ang “daw” pagkatapos ng katinig; parehong nagtatapos sa katinig ang “umalis” at “bukas.”

questions.question: Sa isang ulat, isinulat ng may-akda na “malamang na bumaba ang ani” sa halip na “tiyak na bababa ang ani.” Ano ang pangunahing epekto ng “malamang”?

choices.A: Inaalis nito ang ibang posibleng kinalabasan at inilalahad ang pagbaba bilang tiyak na pangyayari.
choices.B: Ipinakikita nito na naganap na ang pagbaba at iniulat lamang ang naging resulta.
choices.C: Ipinakikitang pagtataya pa lamang ang pagbaba, hindi ganap na katiyakan.
choices.D: Ginagawa nitong tagubilin sa mga magsasaka ang pahayag tungkol sa ani.

questions.note: Ang “malamang” ay nagpapahayag ng posibilidad sa halip na katiyakang ganap nang napatunayan.

questions.question: Sa “Nagpaluto si Lola kay Ana ng pansit bago dumating ang mga bisita,” alin ang wastong pagsusuri sa kilos?

choices.A: Si Lola ang nagluto, dahil siya ang paksa sa pangungusap
choices.B: Si Ana ang aktuwal na nagluto; si Lola ang nag-utos o nagpasagawa ng kilos
choices.C: Hindi matutukoy kung sino ang nagluto dahil dalawang tao ang binanggit
choices.D: Ang mga bisita ang nagluto dahil sila ang dahilan ng paghahanda

questions.note: Ang “nagpaluto” ay nagsasaad na ipinagawa ni Lola kay Ana ang pagluluto; si Ana ang gumagawa ng ipinagawang kilos.

questions.question: Sa “Ikinabahala ng mga iskolar ang pagbura sa mga salitang katutubo,” ano ang papel ng pariralang “ang pagbura sa mga salitang katutubo”?

choices.A: Ito ang tagaganap na nagbura ng mga salita.
choices.B: Ito ang benepisyong natanggap ng mga iskolar.
choices.C: Ito ang sanhi ng pagkabahala.
choices.D: Ito ang taong nakaranas ng pagkabahala.

questions.note: Sa pangungusap, ang pagbura sa mga salitang katutubo ang sanhi ng pagkabahala ng mga iskolar.

questions.question: Sinabi ng tagapagsalaysay, “Mabuti na lamang at naitabi ang mga tala bago bumaha.” Anong saloobin ang idinaragdag ng unang parirala?

choices.A: Nagpapahayag ito ng panghihinayang dahil huli nang nailigtas ang mga tala.
choices.B: Nagpapakita ito ng pagdududa kung may mga tala bago bumaha.
choices.C: Nagpapahayag ito ng ginhawa o pasasalamat dahil naiwasan ang masamang kinalabasan.
choices.D: Nag-uutos ito na itabi ang mga tala sa susunod na pagkakataon.

questions.note: Nagpapahiwatig ang “mabuti na lamang” ng ginhawa o pagkilala sa magandang kinalabasan.

questions.question: Sa “Maaaring makatuwiran ang pasya, subalit hindi naging makatarungan ang proseso,” alin ang pinaghihiwalay ng pahayag?

choices.A: Ipinahihiwatig nitong laging magkasalungat ang pagiging makatuwiran at pagiging makatarungan.
choices.B: Pinag-iiba ang katwiran ng pasya at ang pagiging patas ng prosesong sinunod.
choices.C: Inihahambing nito ang dami ng ebidensiya at haba ng paliwanag sa pasya.
choices.D: Pinag-iiba nito ang legalidad ng pasya at kahusayan ng taong nagpatupad nito.

questions.note: Maaaring pag-ibahin ang resulta ng pasya at ang pagiging makatarungan ng prosesong pinagdaanan.

questions.question: Sa isang salaysay, ang “hiya” ay ginagamit upang ipaliwanag kung bakit tumanggi ang isang tao sa pampublikong papuri. Bakit maaaring kulang ang saling “kahihiyan” lamang?

choices.A: Sa kontekstong ito, ang “hiya” ay tumutukoy lamang sa pribadong damdamin, hindi sa ugnayang panlipunan.
choices.B: Maaaring saklawin ng “hiya” ang paggalang, dangal, ugnayang panlipunan, at pagkapahiya.
choices.C: Ang “hiya” ay mas malapit sa takot sa parusa kaysa sa pagtingin ng kapwa sa ilang konteksto.
choices.D: Ang “hiya” ay palaging nangangahulugan ng paggalang sa nakatatanda, anuman ang sitwasyon.

questions.note: Mas malawak ang saklaw ng “hiya” sa ilang kontekstong panlipunan kaysa sa simpleng “kahihiyan.”

questions.question: Sa isang sitwasyon, pinuri ng lupon ang ambag ni Rosa ngunit hindi siya isinama sa pagdedesisyon. Alin ang pinakamainam na buod ng tensiyon?

choices.A: May pagkilala sa kontribusyon, ngunit hindi kasabay nito ang kapangyarihang makilahok sa pasya.
choices.B: Ang pagkilala sa ambag ay sinamahan ng buong kapangyarihang makilahok sa pagpapasya.
choices.C: Hindi kinilala ang ambag ni Rosa, ngunit ibinigay sa kaniya ang awtoridad na magpasya.
choices.D: Ang suliranin ay hindi ang paglahok sa pasya kundi ang kawalan ng anumang ambag ni Rosa.

questions.note: Maaaring kilalanin ang isang kontribusyon nang hindi ipinagkakaloob ang kapangyarihang makibahagi sa pagpapasya; iyon ang tensiyong ipinapakita sa sitwasyon.

questions.question: Sa isang ulat, ang pariralang “diumano’y kumuha siya ng pondo” ay ginagamit habang wala pang inilalahad na patunay. Ano ang ipinahihiwatig ng “diumano”?

choices.A: Inilalahad ang paratang nang hindi ito lubusang pinagtitibay ng nagsasalita.
choices.B: Tinitiyak na mali ang paratang kaya hindi na kailangang siyasatin.
choices.C: Ipinahihiwatig na napatunayan na ng hukuman ang paratang.
choices.D: Inaatasan ang mambabasa na tanggapin ang paratang bilang katotohanan.

questions.note: Maaaring ipakita ng “diumano” na iniulat ang paratang ngunit hindi pa ito itinuturing na napatunayan sa mismong pahayag.

questions.question: Paghambingin ang “Isinusulat niya ang ulat,” “Isinulat niya ang ulat,” at “Isusulat niya ang ulat.” Ano ang ipinakikita ng mga anyo ng pandiwa?

choices.A: Pagkakaiba sa dami ng taong gumagawa ng kilos
choices.B: Pagkakaiba sa antas ng paggalang sa kausap
choices.C: Pagkakaiba sa pokus ng pandiwa ngunit hindi sa panahon o katayuan ng kilos
choices.D: Pagkakaiba sa aspekto: nagaganap, naganap, at magaganap ang kilos

questions.note: Ipinakikita ng mga anyo ang katayuan ng kilos: nagaganap, naganap, at magaganap.

questions.question: May bugtong na gumagamit ng “bibig” para sa bukana ng isang sisidlan. Bakit hindi sapat ang literal na kahulugan ng salita upang malutas ito?

choices.A: Dapat baligtarin ang kahulugan ng bawat pangngalan upang mahanap ang sagot sa bugtong.
choices.B: Maaaring ilipat ang kahulugan batay sa anyo, gamit, at konteksto ng tinutukoy.
choices.C: Ang “bibig” ay karaniwang literal na tumutukoy lamang sa bahagi ng katawan ng tao.
choices.D: Dapat iwasan ang paghahambing sa tunay na bagay dahil hiwalay ang bugtong sa karaniwang gamit ng salita.

questions.note: Maaaring gamitin nang talinghaga o batay sa pagkakahawig ang isang salita, kaya kailangan ang konteksto upang mahanap ang tinutukoy.

questions.question: Sa “Kahit batid niyang kulang ang oras, ipinagpatuloy niya ang pagsusuri,” ano ang ipinahihiwatig ng “kahit”?

choices.A: Nagpatuloy ang kilos sa kabila ng kalagayang maaaring pumigil dito.
choices.B: Magkapareho ang kahulugan ng dalawang sugnay.
choices.C: Naganap ang pagsusuri bago naging kulang ang oras.
choices.D: Ang kakulangan sa oras ang tuwirang dahilan ng pagtigil.

questions.note: Ipinakikita ng “kahit” ang pagpapatuloy ng kilos sa kabila ng isang salungat na kalagayan.

questions.question: Sa “Hindi man niya tinanggap ang pasya, kinilala niya kung bakit ito pinili,” ano ang papel ng “hindi man”?

choices.A: Ipinahihiwatig na hindi pa nagkaroon ng pagkakataong tanggapin ang pasya.
choices.B: Ipinahihiwatig na tuluyan niyang tinanggap ang pasya sa kabila ng pag-aalinlangan.
choices.C: Itinatanggi na may anumang makatuwirang dahilan sa likod ng pasya.
choices.D: Kinikilala ang isang punto kahit hindi sumasang-ayon sa pasya.

questions.note: Nagpapahayag ang “hindi man” ng pagsang-ayon o pagkilala sa isang bagay sa kabila ng ibang paninindigan.

questions.question: Sa “Hindi ko tinututulan ang kasunduan, kundi ang paraang ipinataw ito,” alin ang pinakamainam na paraphrase?

choices.A: Ang paraan ng pagpapataw ang tinututulan, hindi kinakailangang ang kasunduan mismo.
choices.B: Wala siyang pagtutol sa kasunduan o sa paraang ginamit upang ipatupad ito.
choices.C: Tinatanggap niya ang proseso ngunit pinupuna lamang ang pagsasapubliko nito.
choices.D: Tinututulan niya ang kasunduan, pati ang mga layunin nito at ang paraan ng pagpapatupad.

questions.note: Itinatanggi ng “hindi…kundi…” ang unang maaaring akala at itinatampok ang tunay na pinupuna: ang paraan ng pagpapataw.

questions.question: Paghambingin ang “Nagluto si Mila ng isda” at “Niluto ni Mila ang isda.” Ano ang pinakamahalagang pagkakaiba sa pagbuo ng dalawang pangungusap?

choices.A: Una: magaganap pa lamang ang kilos; ikalawa: naganap na ito.
choices.B: Una: ang isda ang tagaganap; ikalawa: si Mila ang layon ng kilos.
choices.C: Una: walang pandiwa; ikalawa: pang-uri ang pangunahing salita.
choices.D: Si Mila ang tagaganap sa una; ang isda ang layong itinatampok sa ikalawa.

questions.note: Nagkakaiba ang pokus: tagaganap si Mila sa “nagluto,” samantalang ang isda ang layong itinatampok sa “niluto.”

questions.question: Alin ang wastong gamit ng “dahil kay” at “dahil sa” sa dalawang pangungusap?

choices.A: Naantala ang laro dahil kay ulan; nagpasalamat siya dahil kay Ana.
choices.B: Naantala ang laro dahil sa malakas na ulan; nagpasalamat siya dahil kay Ana.
choices.C: Naantala ang laro dahil sa malakas na ulan; nagpasalamat siya dahil sa Ana.
choices.D: Naantala ang laro dahil kay malakas na ulan; nagpasalamat siya dahil sa Ana.

questions.note: Karaniwang ginagamit ang “dahil sa” sa sanhi o bagay gaya ng ulan at “dahil kay” bago ang pangalan ng tao gaya ni Ana.

questions.question: Sinabi ng isang saksi, “Hindi siya sumagot, kaya pumayag siya.” Ano ang pinakamahalagang tanong bago tanggapin ang konklusyon?

choices.A: Naulit ba ang parehong pangungusap nang maraming beses sa salaysay?
choices.B: Alam ba ng saksi ang lahat ng detalye bago pa man magsimula ang pangyayari?
choices.C: Gumamit ba ang saksi ng pormal na pananalita sa kaniyang pahayag?
choices.D: May batayan bang ituring na pagsang-ayon ang katahimikan sa kontekstong ito?

questions.note: Hindi awtomatikong nangangahulugan ng pagsang-ayon ang katahimikan; kailangang suriin ang konteksto at iba pang ebidensiya.

questions.question: Sa pagtalakay sa pagkakamali sa pulong, alin ang nagpapakita ng pagpapakumbaba nang hindi ginagawang kasangkapan ang ibang tao sa pagpapahiya?

choices.A: Itinanggi ng pinuno ang sariling pagkukulang upang mapanatili ang kaniyang awtoridad.
choices.B: Inamin ng pinuno ang sariling pagkukulang at kinilala ang tulong ng iba nang hindi naninisi.
choices.C: Inilahad ng pinuno ang pagkakamali ng kasama upang ipakita ang kaniyang sariling pagiging maingat.
choices.D: Tinanggap ng pinuno ang papuri sa tagumpay ngunit ibinunton sa iba ang pananagutan sa kabiguan.

questions.note: Ang pagpapakumbaba ay pagkilala sa sariling limitasyon at ambag ng iba; naiiba ito sa paggamit ng pagkakamali ng ibang tao upang mapahiya sila.

questions.question: Sa “Kung tutuusin, hindi kakulangan sa datos ang suliranin, kundi ang pagpili kung aling datos ang bibigyang-halaga,” ano ang pinakamahalagang pagbabago sa diin?

choices.A: Mula sa pagsusuri ng ebidensiya tungo sa pag-uulit ng mga pangyayari ayon sa oras.
choices.B: Mula sa pagpapakahulugan tungo sa pagbibilang lamang ng lahat ng nakalap na datos.
choices.C: Mula sa dami ng datos tungo sa paraan ng pagpili at pagbibigay-kahulugan dito.
choices.D: Mula sa pagsasaalang-alang ng ebidensiya tungo sa pag-aakalang walang saysay ang datos.

questions.note: Inililipat ng pahayag ang diin mula sa kakulangan ng datos tungo sa pagpili at pagbibigay-halaga rito.

questions.question: Sa isang tekstong isinulat noong panahon ng kolonyalismo, ginamit ang “bayan” upang tukuyin ang isang pamayanang lokal. Bakit hindi dapat ipagpalagay na kapareho agad ito ng modernong ideya ng bansa?

choices.A: Maaaring magbago ang saklaw ng salita ayon sa panahon, gamit, at konteksto.
choices.B: Ang “bayan” ay palaging tumutukoy sa buong bansang may modernong pambansang soberanya.
choices.C: Mas mainam unawain ang lumang salita ayon sa modernong kahulugan nito bago suriin ang gamit sa teksto.
choices.D: Ang paggamit ng “bayan” sa isang lokal na pamayanan ay nagpapatunay na modernong bansa na ang tinutukoy.

questions.note: Nagbabago ang kahulugan ng mga salita; ang saklaw ng “bayan” sa isang lumang teksto ay dapat unawain ayon sa gamit at panahon nito.

questions.question: Paghambingin ang “Sadyang hindi niya sinabi ang buong katotohanan” at “Hindi niya sinasadyang sabihin ang buong katotohanan.” Ano ang nagbabago?

choices.A: Sa una, sinadya ang hindi pagsasabi; sa ikalawa, hindi sinasadya ang kilos ng pagsasabi.
choices.B: Sa una, tiyak na sinabi niya ang buong katotohanan; sa ikalawa, hindi siya nagsalita.
choices.C: Pareho nilang ipinahihiwatig na aksidenteng hindi naibahagi ang buong katotohanan.
choices.D: Pareho nilang ipinahihiwatig na sinadya niyang itago ang isang bahagi ng katotohanan.

questions.note: Nagbabago ang saklaw ng “sadyang”: sa una, tuwirang inilalarawan ang sinadyang hindi pagsasabi; sa ikalawa, ang pagsasabi ang kilos na hindi nilayon.

questions.question: May nagsabing, “Totoo ang pahayag dahil matagal na itong salawikain.” Ano ang pinakamalakas na pagsusuri sa pangangatwirang ito?

choices.A: Ihambing ang salawikain sa ibang kasabihan at ituring ang pagkakasundo ng mga ito bilang patunay.
choices.B: Nagiging kapantay ng estadistikang datos ang salawikain kapag malawak itong ginagamit sa komunidad.
choices.C: Suriin kung ang aral ay angkop sa konklusyon at kung may hiwalay na ebidensiya.
choices.D: Sapat ang katandaan at pag-uulit ng salawikain upang patunayan ang anumang pahayag.

questions.note: Hindi sapat na tradisyonal ang isang pahayag upang patunayan ang konklusyon; kailangan ang kaugnayan at sapat na batayan.

questions.question: Isinalin ang isang pormal na pakiusap bilang tuwirang utos. Kahit malapit ang literal na kahulugan, ano ang pinakamalamang na nawala?

choices.A: Lahat ng kahulugang taglay ng pandiwa ay nawawala kapag ginawang tuwiran ang pakiusap.
choices.B: Ang antas ng paggalang at ugnayan ng nagsasalita sa kausap.
choices.C: Ang pormal na pakiusap ay laging nagiging tanong tungkol sa paksa, hindi utos.
choices.D: Ang ayos ng salita lamang, kahit magkapareho ang tono at pakikitungo.

questions.note: May kahulugan ang rehistro at antas ng paggalang; maaaring magbago ang dating ng pahayag kahit malapit ang literal na salin.

questions.question: Why did the Roman Republic develop checks such as separate magistracies and a Senate?

choices.A: To transfer military decisions to provincial assemblies
choices.B: To limit concentrated power among rival offices and elites
choices.C: To broaden citizenship while retaining important social exclusions
choices.D: To replace hereditary monarchy with an elected emperor

questions.note: Republican institutions distributed authority, though political equality remained limited.

questions.question: Which ship sank in 1912 after striking an iceberg?

choices.A: Mayflower
choices.B: Lusitania
choices.C: Britannic
choices.D: Titanic

questions.note: The Titanic struck an iceberg and sank in April 1912; the Lusitania was torpedoed in 1915, and the Britannic sank in 1916.

questions.question: Whose 1492 voyage reached the Americas for Spain?

choices.A: Christopher Columbus
choices.B: Vasco da Gama
choices.C: Ferdinand Magellan
choices.D: Amerigo Vespucci

questions.note: Da Gama sailed to India for Portugal; Magellan's voyage began in 1519.

questions.question: In which country did the Renaissance begin?

choices.A: England
choices.B: France
choices.C: Spain
choices.D: Italy

questions.note: It began in Italian city-states like Florence in the 14th century.

questions.question: Who led Nazi Germany during World War II?

choices.A: Adolf Hitler
choices.B: Benito Mussolini
choices.C: Kaiser Wilhelm II
choices.D: Otto von Bismarck

questions.note: Mussolini led Fascist Italy; Bismarck and Wilhelm II were earlier German leaders.

questions.question: Which civilization built Machu Picchu?

choices.A: Olmec
choices.B: Maya
choices.C: Inca
choices.D: Aztec

questions.note: Built in the Peruvian Andes in the 15th century.

questions.question: Which ancient civilization built the pyramids at Giza?

choices.A: Sumerians
choices.B: Egyptians
choices.C: Persians
choices.D: Phoenicians

questions.note: Built during Egypt's Old Kingdom, c. 2600–2500 BC.

questions.question: Which war ended in 1945?

choices.A: World War II
choices.B: Korean War
choices.C: Vietnam War
choices.D: World War I

questions.note: WWI ended 1918, Korea 1953 (armistice), Vietnam 1975.

questions.question: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?

choices.A: Yuri Gagarin
choices.B: John Glenn
choices.C: Neil Armstrong
choices.D: Buzz Aldrin

questions.note: Apollo 11, 1969. Gagarin was the first human in space (1961).

questions.question: Which empire did Genghis Khan found?

choices.A: Timurid Empire
choices.B: Mongol Empire
choices.C: Ottoman Empire
choices.D: Mughal Empire

questions.note: Founded in 1206.

questions.question: Why is comparing tax records with personal diaries often more useful than relying on either source alone?

choices.A: Diaries usually provide a statistically representative sample of the whole population
choices.B: The two sources generally record the same details in different formats
choices.C: Tax records usually capture private motives more directly than diaries, because they explain why each household accepted a policy.
choices.D: Different source types can show both administrative priorities and some private experiences

questions.note: Tax records and diaries have different purposes and biases; comparing them can reveal what each source does and does not show.

questions.question: How did printing help the Protestant Reformation spread?

choices.A: It helped standardize doctrine across competing Protestant groups
choices.B: It lowered the cost and sped up the circulation of religious texts
choices.C: It made vernacular preaching less important than written debate
choices.D: It reduced religious disagreement in regions with many printed texts

questions.note: Printing amplified circulation; it did not mechanically guarantee uniform belief.

questions.question: Why did the Black Death affect European regions differently?

choices.A: Demography, trade routes, local institutions, and public responses varied among regions
choices.B: Climate alone determined mortality regardless of population movement or living conditions
choices.C: Trade networks had no role once the disease entered a region
choices.D: The disease strain was identical, so survival rates must have been the same everywhere

questions.note: Mortality and social consequences varied with population structure, connectivity, institutions, and local conditions.

questions.question: Why does the existence of a citizen assembly alone not prove that an ancient Greek polis was democratic in a modern inclusive sense?

choices.A: Some poleis used assemblies, while others limited participation through different institutions
choices.B: Ancient assemblies did not make decisions about public affairs
choices.C: Women, enslaved people, and resident foreigners could be excluded from political membership
choices.D: Written laws generally ensured that every resident could participate equally once an assembly existed.

questions.note: Participation depended on citizenship rules that excluded substantial parts of the population.

questions.question: How could postwar inflation weaken some governments after World War I?

choices.A: It mainly affected import prices, leaving domestic savings and wages unchanged
choices.B: It could erode savings and wages, intensify distributional conflict, and reduce trust in institutions
choices.C: Debt relief could ease pressure on some households without ending wider political conflict
choices.D: It reliably raised purchasing power for wage earners as fast as prices rose

questions.note: Inflation can undermine savings and purchasing power and intensify disputes over wages, prices, and state credibility.

questions.question: Why is technological superiority alone an incomplete explanation for imperial conquest?

choices.A: Maritime technology mattered alongside finance, labor, and state power in many empires
choices.B: Military technology had no influence on any imperial campaign
choices.C: A technological edge guaranteed victory regardless of terrain or local alliances
choices.D: Outcomes also depended on logistics, disease, alliances, local politics, and state capacity

questions.note: Conquest depended on multiple interacting factors, not technology alone.

questions.question: Which broad pattern best describes decolonization after World War II?

choices.A: Independence came at different times through negotiation, mass movements, and sometimes prolonged conflict
choices.B: Most colonies became independent through an identical process by 1947
choices.C: Nationalist movements generally faded once wartime economies recovered
choices.D: Decolonization followed different routes, but African colonies generally gained independence before Asian colonies.

questions.note: Decolonization unfolded unevenly across regions and involved different mixes of negotiation, resistance, and international pressure.

questions.question: How should historians assess a leader's claim that conquest brought 'civilization'?

choices.A: Treat the claim as propaganda and dismiss any material changes it describes
choices.B: Compare it with policy and the experiences of conquered people
choices.C: Use the leader’s stated intentions as the main evidence of the outcome
choices.D: Judge the claim chiefly by the roads, schools, and offices constructed

questions.note: Imperial rhetoric should be tested against evidence and affected populations.

questions.question: Why can the legal abolition of slavery differ from freedom in practice?

choices.A: Debt, coercion, discrimination, and landlessness may persist after abolition
choices.B: Formal freedom generally removed the economic barriers faced by formerly enslaved people
choices.C: Enslavement was usually enforced through custom rather than law
choices.D: Formal abolition usually ended coercive labor and economic dependency at once, even where social status remained unequal.

questions.note: Formal emancipation does not automatically dismantle coercive structures.

questions.question: Historical knowledge check: Which document begins with 'We the People'?

choices.A: Declaration of Independence
choices.B: Emancipation Proclamation
choices.C: U.S. Constitution
choices.D: Magna Carta

questions.note: The Declaration begins 'When in the Course of human events'.

questions.question: Why did national unification help some countries industrialize without making industrialization automatic?

choices.A: It mattered mainly after factories were established, rather than shaping early industrial growth.
choices.B: It made industrial growth largely independent of transport networks, finance, energy, and technology.
choices.C: It reduced some trade barriers, while capital, labor, energy, and technology still mattered.
choices.D: It lowered trade barriers but did little to expand markets or coordinate investment across regions.

questions.note: Larger integrated markets could support specialization, but industrialization also depended on resources, finance, labor, technology, and institutions.

questions.question: Which interpretation best explains how the Treaty of Versailles contributed to later instability without making World War II inevitable?

choices.A: Its terms created grievances that political leaders later exploited during economic and institutional crises
choices.B: Its provisions contributed to disputes, but Germany’s recovery made the settlement less important to politics over time.
choices.C: Its recognition of national self-determination resolved most disputes over borders and minority populations.
choices.D: Its military restrictions mattered, while reparations and territorial changes had little effect on later political debate.

questions.note: The treaty created grievances, but the later war depended on choices and developments including the Great Depression, Nazi expansion, and failures of collective security.

questions.question: Which example best illustrates why the Cold War could be both a superpower rivalry and a series of local conflicts?

choices.A: Local leaders pursued their own aims while rival blocs supplied weapons, money, or advisers.
choices.B: The superpowers mainly fought direct conventional battles against each other in Europe.
choices.C: Outside support usually erased local political goals and made conflicts identical.
choices.D: Most regional wars stayed separate from the Cold War’s alliances and ideological competition.

questions.note: Proxy conflicts often combined local causes with outside support; neither superpower directly fought the other in a full-scale war.

questions.question: Why is a purely economic explanation of the French Revolution incomplete?

choices.A: Fiscal pressures mattered, but hardship was largely confined to towns and did not shape rural discontent.
choices.B: Fiscal strain and food prices interacted with privilege, political conflict, and Enlightenment ideas.
choices.C: The monarchy’s debt crisis became important only after the Estates-General met, rather than shaping the decision to summon it.
choices.D: Enlightenment ideas circulated among elites but contributed little to how political grievances were expressed in 1789.

questions.note: The fiscal crisis and hardship mattered, but social privilege, political authority, and new ideas shaped how crisis became revolution.

questions.question: Which chain of effects best captures the Atlantic slave trade as an economic system?

choices.A: European merchants profited, but plantation labor remained secondary to Atlantic trade.
choices.B: Forced migration reshaped African societies, while plantation output mattered little to commerce.
choices.C: Plantation exports generated wealth but remained separate from credit, insurance, and shipping.
choices.D: Coerced labor supported plantation exports tied to shipping, insurance, credit, and commerce.

questions.note: The trade linked African forced migration, plantation production in the Americas, and commercial networks across the Atlantic.

questions.question: After the Ottoman Empire dissolved, why did the borders of several successor states remain contested?

choices.A: Wartime promises and local nationalist claims generally aligned, allowing successor states to agree on borders quickly.
choices.B: Most new borders followed locally organized votes held after the armistice, with little influence from outside powers.
choices.C: Wartime promises, mandates, local movements, and imperial interests did not always align
choices.D: Outside powers shaped formal agreements, but local movements generally agreed on the same political boundaries.

questions.note: Postwar state formation reflected competing local aspirations and decisions by outside powers, especially through mandates.

questions.question: Why did revolutionary ideas spread unevenly across the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries?

choices.A: Print carried ideas across borders, but censorship and limited literacy kept most political arguments within royal courts.
choices.B: Ideas traveled through print, war, trade, and migration, then were adapted to local struggles
choices.C: Revolutionary ideas crossed borders with little change, so local institutions mainly affected when they were adopted.
choices.D: Political ideas spread chiefly through official diplomacy; war, trade, and migration played a minor role.

questions.note: Communication networks carried ideas across borders, but local institutions, interests, and conditions shaped how they were used.

questions.question: A German army has failed to take a major Soviet city, suffered a catastrophic surrender, and lost initiative in the east. What broader change does this best indicate?

choices.A: The battle showed that Allied material support had already made Germany’s defeat certain before the Soviet counteroffensive.
choices.B: Germany captured the city and opened a secure route toward the Caucasus oil fields.
choices.C: The battle led the Soviet Union to suspend its offensive and redirect most of its effort toward the Pacific.
choices.D: Germany was increasingly forced to respond to Soviet advances rather than set the pace in the east

questions.note: Stalingrad was a major strategic turning point: Germany lost a large force and the Red Army increasingly drove the eastern campaign.

questions.question: A Soviet reform program encourages more open public discussion while another seeks to restructure the economy. Which pairing best matches those aims?

choices.A: Perestroika for openness; détente for restructuring
choices.B: Glasnost for openness; perestroika for restructuring
choices.C: Détente for openness; collectivization for restructuring
choices.D: Collectivization for openness; glasnost for restructuring

questions.note: Glasnost refers to openness, while perestroika refers to restructuring; détente describes easing international tensions.

questions.question: A textbook dates the end of the Western Roman Empire to 476. Which qualification makes that date more historically precise?

choices.A: The western emperor was deposed, while the eastern Roman state continued.
choices.B: It marks Rome’s first sack and the permanent end of imperial rule in both halves.
choices.C: It marks the fall of Constantinople to the Ottomans, ending the eastern empire in 1453.
choices.D: It marks the transfer of the imperial capital to Constantinople, which happened centuries earlier.

questions.note: The deposition of Romulus Augustulus is a conventional marker for the Western Empire’s end, not the disappearance of all Roman institutions or the Eastern Empire.

questions.question: The Congress of Vienna restored dynasties but later faced revolutions in Europe. Which explanation best reconciles those outcomes?

choices.A: It restored dynasties while expanding political participation enough to remove most liberal opposition.
choices.B: It emphasized dynastic legitimacy and balance of power, while later revolutions drew on unresolved social and national conflicts.
choices.C: It ended major-power competition in Europe, so later revolutions developed largely outside the system it created.
choices.D: It restored a balance of power, but could not remove nationalism, liberalism, or social grievances

questions.note: The settlement aimed to restore stability and balance; it did not erase political ideas or the pressures behind later revolutions.

questions.question: Two regions of the Western Roman Empire faced invasions, but only one also suffered severe fiscal strain and repeated internal power struggles. What does this comparison support?

choices.A: External migration explains the changes well without considering the state’s ability to raise resources.
choices.B: The same military pressure could have different effects depending on fiscal and political capacity.
choices.C: Internal power struggles became important mainly near the final collapse of the western court.
choices.D: The western region’s fiscal strain mattered less than the invaders’ numbers in both regions.

questions.note: Comparing regions helps distinguish external pressure from the internal conditions that shaped resilience.

questions.question: A new African state inherits a colonial boundary that divides one community and places rival communities under the same government. Which consequence is most plausible, though not inevitable?

choices.A: Recognition of the border would likely prevent cross-border trade and political ties from developing.
choices.B: The inherited boundary itself determined political competition, regardless of how later institutions or bargains developed.
choices.C: The new border would quickly replace older community identities with a single national identity.
choices.D: Political competition may be shaped by mismatched borders and existing local identities.

questions.note: Colonial boundaries sometimes divided connected communities or grouped competing ones, interacting with later politics rather than mechanically causing conflict.

questions.question: An imperial report praises a railway for increasing exports but never mentions compulsory labor used to build it. What is the most defensible source criticism?

choices.A: The report may describe export growth accurately while leaving coercion and its costs out of view.
choices.B: The omission makes the export figures unusable even if other records support the reported increase.
choices.C: Compulsory labor means the railway’s export contribution should be treated as negative rather than assessed separately.
choices.D: Because the report was written by imperial officials, its output measures can be assumed neutral even when labor is omitted.

questions.note: A source may provide useful evidence about output while its purpose and omissions shape the picture it presents.

questions.question: The Taiping Rebellion weakened Qing authority and caused enormous loss of life. Which conclusion is best supported by those effects?

choices.A: The Qing survived, but the rebellion exposed severe internal strain and weakened the state.
choices.B: The rebellion forced the Qing court to establish a republic before the dynasty’s formal fall.
choices.C: The rebellion reduced the court’s reliance on regional armies and strengthened centralized control over the provinces.
choices.D: The conflict arose mainly from cross-border rivalry, with domestic religious and social grievances playing a limited role.

questions.note: The rebellion was a massive internal conflict that damaged the Qing state but did not itself overthrow the dynasty.

questions.question: Why did Japan’s carrier losses at Midway matter beyond the ships themselves?

choices.A: Japan replaced its lost carrier aircrews quickly enough to retain the initiative in the central Pacific.
choices.B: Japan lost experienced naval air power, and the initiative increasingly shifted toward the United States.
choices.C: The battle disrupted Japanese operations, but its main effect was on shipping rather than carrier-based air power.
choices.D: The carrier losses reduced Japan’s striking power, but did not seriously affect the balance of power in the central Pacific.

questions.note: The battle inflicted major carrier and aircrew losses on Japan and helped shift strategic initiative, though the war continued for years.

questions.question: Britain entered World War I after Germany invaded Belgium. Which chain most directly links the invasion to Britain’s decision?

choices.A: Britain’s decision was based on a prior promise to enter any war involving France, whether or not Belgium was invaded.
choices.B: Germany violated Belgian neutrality, and Britain had a treaty-backed interest in defending it.
choices.C: Britain entered primarily after German attacks on British colonies in Africa, rather than because of events in Belgium.
choices.D: Belgian neutrality was noted diplomatically, but it carried no treaty or strategic weight in Britain’s decision.

questions.note: The invasion of neutral Belgium was a major factor in Britain’s declaration of war, alongside broader strategic concerns.

questions.question: Germany’s 1923 hyperinflation intensified during the Ruhr occupation. Which explanation best links the occupation to the currency crisis?

choices.A: The occupation interrupted industrial output, while tax revenue remained sufficient to avoid monetary expansion.
choices.B: The government restricted credit to pay for passive resistance, which reduced prices but weakened production.
choices.C: The government financed passive resistance and obligations by expanding the money supply.
choices.D: Foreign loans covered most passive-resistance costs, leaving monetary policy a minor part of the crisis.

questions.note: During the Ruhr crisis, financing passive resistance through money creation compounded existing fiscal and monetary problems.

questions.question: Tokugawa restrictions on foreign contact targeted some European traders and Christian missions while allowing selected commerce. What does that pattern suggest?

choices.A: The shogunate tried to manage foreign contact as a political and religious risk, not end every exchange.
choices.B: The policy left little room for imported knowledge or regulated trade with overseas partners.
choices.C: Restrictions mainly followed demands from Qing China after a Japanese military defeat.
choices.D: The shogunate applied mostly uniform restrictions, with few differences by port or trading status.

questions.note: The Tokugawa system restricted contacts thought to threaten political order, especially Christian missions, while maintaining controlled exchanges.

questions.question: Napoleon’s sale of Louisiana followed French setbacks in Saint-Domingue and renewed conflict with Britain. Which interpretation best connects those events?

choices.A: The sale mainly funded a planned French invasion of British Canada, with Louisiana serving as collateral.
choices.B: France planned to retain Louisiana as a Caribbean supply base despite its weakening position in Saint-Domingue.
choices.C: The loss of prospects in the Caribbean and need for funds made a distant territory less useful to France
choices.D: Napoleon sold the territory chiefly to prevent U.S. settlers from moving west while France kept the Mississippi.

questions.note: After the Haitian Revolution undermined France’s Caribbean ambitions, Napoleon sold Louisiana and gained funds as war with Britain approached.

questions.question: Which evidence would best challenge the claim that one invention alone caused Britain’s Industrial Revolution?

choices.A: One inventor received a patent before large-scale factory production became common.
choices.B: A single steam-engine improvement preceded the growth of factories in one region.
choices.C: Britain’s industrialization combined changes in energy, labor, finance, transport, and markets.
choices.D: Factory output increased after machinery changed, without showing that machinery alone caused it.

questions.note: A systemic explanation accounts for technological change alongside labor, capital, resources, and institutions.

questions.question: A country wins independence but remains dependent on one former colonial market, foreign loans, and imported fuel. What distinction does this illustrate?

choices.A: Economic dependence usually requires foreign officials to control domestic administration.
choices.B: Continued trade with the former colonial market means legal independence was incomplete.
choices.C: Diplomatic recognition normally removes external constraints on a country’s policy choices.
choices.D: A country can be legally independent yet constrained by debt, trade dependence, and imported fuel.

questions.note: Formal sovereignty and economic autonomy are different dimensions; trade, debt, and security relationships may persist after independence.

questions.question: The French Revolution proclaimed universal rights, while Saint-Domingue’s enslaved population fought for emancipation. What contradiction did the Haitian Revolution expose?

choices.A: The revolution concerned local administration but did not challenge the meaning of universal rights.
choices.B: The Haitian Revolution mainly sought to preserve plantation slavery while changing trade rules.
choices.C: Universal-rights rhetoric clashed with the failure to apply equal rights to enslaved people in the colonies.
choices.D: French leaders had already agreed on equal rights for enslaved people before the Haitian uprising.

questions.note: The Haitian Revolution forced the meaning of liberty and equality to confront slavery and colonial rule.

questions.question: A government changes census categories and then uses them to distribute representation and public services. Which inference is most defensible?

choices.A: Census categories can shape representation and services instead of merely recording identity.
choices.B: The labels affect policy mainly when residents actively organize around them.
choices.C: The categories mostly record identities that were already fixed before the census.
choices.D: Changes in representation follow population growth, not decisions about classification.

questions.note: Censuses measure populations but their categories and uses can affect representation, resource allocation, and social recognition.

questions.question: Two countries experience a severe economic depression. One sees an authoritarian movement gain power; the other preserves competitive democracy. What comparison would best explain the difference?

choices.A: Compare the countries’ size and population first, assuming political institutions respond similarly to economic shocks.
choices.B: Compare institutions, party systems, elite decisions, and public trust before and during the crisis.
choices.C: Treat public trust as a consequence of the depression, rather than a condition that could shape political responses.
choices.D: Attribute the contrast mainly to differences in when the recession began, without examining parties or elite choices.

questions.note: Economic crisis shapes opportunities and grievances, but institutions, political choices, and social coalitions affect outcomes.

questions.question: After the Meiji Restoration, Japan adopted foreign technology while changing taxation, education, military service, and government institutions. Which interpretation best explains the speed of its transformation?

choices.A: Japan combined imported techniques with institutional reforms that helped mobilize resources and coordinate change.
choices.B: Foreign technology alone drove modernization, while domestic institutions and state capacity remained largely unchanged.
choices.C: The reforms mainly restored the independent authority of daimyo, reducing the central government’s ability to act.
choices.D: Industrial growth came first, and the government changed education, taxation, and military service only after modernization was complete.

questions.note: The Meiji state did not merely import machines; it also reorganized institutions that supported rapid political, military, and economic change.

questions.question: An Egyptian royal inscription celebrates a major monument. Which evidence would best help a historian assess what that achievement meant for ordinary workers?

choices.A: Royal inscriptions describing construction provide a reliable account of workers’ daily living conditions.
choices.B: Labor records, settlement remains, skeletal evidence, and provisioning records can reveal workers’ conditions.
choices.C: The monument’s scale alone establishes how many workers were paid and whether their labor was voluntary.
choices.D: Later artistic depictions are the strongest evidence because they record working arrangements without political framing.

questions.note: Royal inscriptions reveal how rulers presented their achievements; labor records, settlements, skeletal remains, and provisioning evidence can better illuminate workers’ lives.

questions.question: After the Reichstag Fire, the Nazi government used emergency powers. Which development most clearly shows how the crisis helped consolidate dictatorship?

choices.A: Civil liberties were suspended and opponents were easier to arrest or suppress
choices.B: Emergency powers were renewed, but parliamentary checks continued to block major restrictions on opposition activity.
choices.C: The decree was mainly an economic stabilization measure, while opposition parties continued operating openly.
choices.D: The crisis strengthened Nazi influence, but courts and political parties continued to constrain the government effectively.

questions.note: The fire was used to justify emergency restrictions and weaken organized opposition, helping consolidate Nazi rule.

questions.question: The Berlin Wall opened in November 1989; German reunification followed in October 1990. What does this sequence most strongly suggest?

choices.A: The border opening was largely symbolic because legal reunification had already taken place before it.
choices.B: Opening the border accelerated change, but legal reunification still required political negotiation and agreement.
choices.C: Reunification occurred automatically when border controls ended, and later agreements merely recorded that change.
choices.D: The two events were largely unrelated because international diplomacy played little role in German reunification.

questions.note: The wall’s opening accelerated political change, but reunification required a separate legal and diplomatic process.

questions.question: Why did Magna Carta become historically influential even though it did not create modern democracy in 1215?

choices.A: It transferred final policymaking authority from the king to an elected parliament with a broad franchise.
choices.B: It established the principle of popular sovereignty through a nationally elected assembly in 1215.
choices.C: It made the right to vote broadly equal across social classes, even though later parliaments remained limited.
choices.D: Later constitutional traditions used Magna Carta as a symbol of limits on royal power.

questions.note: Magna Carta was limited in its original context, but later generations invoked it in debates over lawful limits on rulers.

questions.question: A historian argues that empire-building was driven only by commercial profit. Which finding would most directly weaken that explanation?

choices.A: A minister praised trade after expansion, without explaining the decision to expand.
choices.B: One colony’s exports rose during a profitable decade, consistent with a profit motive.
choices.C: Security fears, strategic rivalry, and ideology shaped expansion even where profit was uncertain.
choices.D: The empire controlled several ports, which demonstrates access to trade but not the chief motive.

questions.note: A monocausal argument is weakened by evidence of independent motives and cases where expansion cannot be explained by expected profit alone.

questions.question: Why do historians criticize accounts that present European global dominance as an inevitable result of Europe’s internal development?

choices.A: Exchange, colonial extraction, other regions, and contingent events also shaped Europe’s rise.
choices.B: The criticism rejects regional comparison because societies follow unique paths.
choices.C: The account treats global trade as a result of European expansion rather than a network already linking regions.
choices.D: The argument discounts European institutions and technologies instead of studying their interaction with power.

questions.note: Global-history approaches challenge inevitability by examining connected development, extraction, exchange, and historical contingency.

questions.question: A food-price crisis precedes a revolution, but grievances and political exclusion had developed for decades. Which analysis best distinguishes trigger from structural cause?

choices.A: Long-term grievances created vulnerability; the immediate crisis helped turn it into action.
choices.B: Long-term grievances explain the outbreak’s timing without considering the immediate crisis.
choices.C: The event nearest to a revolution should receive the greatest causal weight.
choices.D: The food-price crisis is structural mainly because it happened close to the outbreak.

questions.note: Structural causes explain persistent vulnerability; a trigger helps explain timing without making the outcome inevitable.

questions.question: A law formally abolishes forced labor, but inspectors continue to report coercive contracts and unpaid obligations. What is the strongest historical conclusion?

choices.A: Ongoing coercion in some inspected areas proves abolition failed everywhere, even without evidence from other regions.
choices.B: Once the law changed, later labor practices should be analyzed separately rather than used to assess enforcement.
choices.C: Formal abolition should be judged chiefly by its legal language, while unpaid obligations are a different economic issue.
choices.D: Legal abolition changed formal status, but enforcement and economic dependence need separate analysis.

questions.note: Abolition can change legal status without ending coercive practices; enforcement and economic dependence must be examined separately.

questions.question: A nationalist movement claims to speak for all citizens, yet its records show disputes over land, language, and regional power. What interpretation best fits the evidence?

choices.A: Disputes over land, language, and regional power show that nationalist goals were mostly rhetorical throughout the movement.
choices.B: A shared national goal can coexist with competing views of land, language, and political power.
choices.C: The disagreements were probably procedural, so they tell historians little about the movement’s social priorities.
choices.D: A shared independence goal means internal conflicts over land and language can be treated as secondary details.

questions.note: Nationalist movements can share broad goals while containing important disagreements over who benefits, which identities are represented, and how power should be distributed.

questions.question: A local revolution occurs during a global credit crisis and a war among empires. Which approach best uses global history without erasing local agency?

choices.A: Explain local decisions mainly as reactions to foreign governments’ priorities.
choices.B: Use overseas diplomatic records alone because they cover several countries at once.
choices.C: Set global conditions aside once evidence of local grievances has been found.
choices.D: Trace how global pressures changed local options while examining choices made by local actors.

questions.note: Global context can alter resources and opportunities, but local actors interpret and respond to those pressures.

questions.question: A government declares a literacy campaign successful because enrollment rose. Which additional evidence is most necessary to evaluate the claim fairly?

choices.A: Learning outcomes, attendance, completion, regional access, and comparison with the stated goals
choices.B: Use enrollment alone to establish success on the stated goal, even when attendance and learning remain uncertain.
choices.C: Measure completion rates only, since literacy assessments and regional access are separate from campaign success.
choices.D: Judge the campaign chiefly by money spent and classrooms opened rather than by student outcomes.

questions.note: Assessment requires explicit criteria and evidence about participation and outcomes, not merely one output measure.

questions.question: Why is attributing World War II solely to Hitler’s intentions an incomplete explanation?

choices.A: Geography explains military outcomes with little need to examine industrial or political choices.
choices.B: Institutions, other governments, industry, alliances, and decisions across theaters shaped the war.
choices.C: Leadership decisions mattered chiefly before alliance coordination became central to the war.
choices.D: Economic resources and alliances shaped strategy mainly after the major fighting had ended.

questions.note: Hitler’s decisions were central but cannot alone explain the war’s causes, global expansion, or outcome.

questions.question: Athens and Sparta shared a Greek language and religious traditions but organized citizenship and military life differently. What does this comparison show?

choices.A: Athenian democracy became the standard model adopted by most Greek city-states.
choices.B: A shared Greek culture did not require identical political institutions or civic priorities.
choices.C: Shared religious traditions encouraged broadly similar citizenship rules across the Greek world.
choices.D: Their differences emerged mainly after Roman rule reshaped Greek political life.

questions.note: Greek identity coexisted with substantial variation among city-states in institutions, social structures, and military priorities.

questions.question: A historian wants to test whether New Zealand’s 1893 women’s suffrage reform led to broader political equality, rather than only formal voting access. Which evidence would best serve that purpose?

choices.A: Compare election turnout in one year without examining candidacy rules or barriers to participation.
choices.B: Count newspaper celebrations of the reform and treat public attention as evidence of equal influence.
choices.C: Compare voting rights with candidacy access, participation, and policy influence over time.
choices.D: Treat the national suffrage law as sufficient proof that other political barriers had ended.

questions.note: New Zealand’s 1893 reform was a major milestone in women’s parliamentary voting rights, but assessing broader equality requires evidence beyond the law itself.

choices.A: Peru
choices.B: Colombia
choices.C: Argentina
choices.D: Brazil

questions.note: Brazil has over 200 million people.

choices.B: Karakoram
choices.C: Himalayas
choices.D: Andes

choices.A: Kalahari
choices.B: Gobi
choices.C: Arabian
choices.D: Sahara

choices.C: Portugal
choices.D: Greece

choices.A: San Marino

choices.C: Monaco
choices.D: Liechtenstein

questions.question: Why can a country's population density be high near a river delta?

choices.A: Deltas usually sit above surrounding floodplains, so flood management plays little role in their settlement patterns.
choices.B: Deltas tend to be isolated from inland and maritime trade routes because channels are too unstable for transport.
choices.C: Flat, fertile land and transport access support settlement
choices.D: Deltas offer fertile land, but settlement density is low because farming is rarely possible on deposited sediments.

questions.note: Deltas offer agricultural and transport advantages but also serious environmental risks.

questions.question: Which country does NOT border Germany?

choices.A: Italy
choices.B: Poland
choices.C: Austria
choices.D: Denmark

questions.note: Austria and Switzerland separate Germany from Italy.

questions.question: Mount Kilimanjaro is in which country?

choices.A: Uganda
choices.B: Tanzania
choices.C: Ethiopia
choices.D: Kenya

questions.note: It sits near the Kenyan border but inside Tanzania.

questions.question: Which body of water lies between Saudi Arabia and northeast Africa?

choices.A: Red Sea
choices.B: Caspian Sea
choices.C: Persian Gulf
choices.D: Arabian Sea

choices.A: California

choices.C: Montana

choices.B: Baltic Sea

questions.question: Geography challenge: Which north–south range forms much of the conventional Europe–Asia boundary?

choices.A: Altai Mountains
choices.B: Ural Mountains
choices.C: Carpathian Mountains
choices.D: Caucasus Mountains

questions.note: The Caucasus run east–west further south.

choices.A: Madagascar
choices.B: Borneo
choices.C: New Guinea
choices.D: Greenland
